results.answer:
Stopping at class level during validation occurs when the `ClassLevelCascadeMode` is set to `CascadeMode.Stop` and a rule within the validator generates one or more failures [1].

This causes the validation process to halt, preventing further rules from being executed [1].

Stopping within a property rule during validation occurs when the `CascadeMode` for a specific property rule is set to `CascadeMode.Stop` and that rule generates one or more failures [2].

This causes the validation process to halt for that particular property, but other properties may still be validated [2].

The difference between stopping at class level and stopping within a property rule is that the former halts all further validation, while the latter only stops validation for the specific property where the failure occurred, allowing other properties to be validated [1] [2].
